clue.text: Croupiers' behaviour at banquet?

parts.note: croupiers work at gaming tables, so their conduct is jokingly the etiquette of the table, which is also how one should behave when dining

explanation.surface: Wondering how casino staff conduct themselves at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette when eating is proper conduct at a meal, and the phrase puns on the gaming tables croupiers run.

clue.text: Historian understood you and me

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: A historian grasped what we were talking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman writer of the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Pill for old athlete when record round disqualified

indicators.note: disqualified suggests some of the athlete being struck out, here the record and the round

parts.note: the Discobolus is the famous ancient Greek statue of a discus thrower
a disc is a gramophone record
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A drug was found on a veteran sportsman disqualified after a record lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disqualified' strips DISC and O from DISCOBOLUS, the ancient discus-thrower of Myron's statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolus is a large pill, especially one given to animals.

clue.text: Antony's friend sent back one horse to America

indicators.note: sent back means the word one is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: a barb is a Barbary horse, a breed from North Africa
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A friend of Mark Antony returns a horse to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Enobarbus is Mark Antony's loyal follower in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Alcoholic radical may be converted Liberal

indicators.note: be converted signals the letters of may being changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A hard-drinking extremist might switch to the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be converted' rearranges MAY into AMY. In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms, and amyl is found in amyl alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Amyl is the five-carbon chemical group present in amyl alcohol.

clue.text: Unnecessary fit of nerves when afloat

parts.note: the needle is British slang for nervous tension before a contest
SS, steamship, prefixes the names of vessels on the water

explanation.surface: Seasickness and jitters on board were pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means without need, so not required.

clue.text: Recommendation to jockey

definitions.meaning: a note added to a jury's verdict suggesting a course of action
someone who sits on and races a horse

explanation.surface: Advice given to the person riding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both a recommendation appended to a verdict and one who rides.

clue.text: VIP is in large-scale racket

parts.note: big means large in scale
a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A very important person is involved in a major fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a criminal scheme, but it is a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A big noise is informal for a person of importance.

clue.text: Directions to reinstate lines in what Dobson meant as an ode

definitions.text: lines in what Dobson meant as an ode

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are compass directions
stet is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to restore a deleted word

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting back verses into a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin Dobson was a Victorian poet who wrote in strict French and Italian verse forms; the sonnet ends in six lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is the closing group of six verses in a sonnet.

clue.text: Print, having no second copy to sell perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of copy and to sell may be arranged in some other way
having no tells us to take a letter away from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A print that cannot be sold because no duplicate was made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes S (second) from COPY TO SELL, leaving COPYTOELL, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A collotype is a type of photomechanical print made from a gelatine plate.

clue.text: Send cards for many players

definitions.meaning: to send something, such as a ball, hard on its way
a whist ... is a social event where many people play cards

explanation.surface: Dealing out the cards for a big group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means propel or dispatch, and a whist drive is a card-playing gathering for many tables.

clue.text: In the ranks he was almost cheerful

definitions.text: In the ranks he was almost cheerful

parts.words: In the ranks he was almost cheerful
parts.note: alludes to Macaulay's poem Horatius, in which even the soldiers of the opposing Etrurian army could scarce forbear to cheer at the hero's bravery on the bridge

explanation.surface: A soldier in the ranks who was nearly in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay's Horatius, a famous Victorian ballad, says 'even the ranks of Tuscany could scarce forbear to cheer'; one of those soldiers almost cheered.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Tuscany stood in the ranks of the Etruscan army that, in the poem, nearly cheered its foe.

clue.text: Instrument fashionable in Bordeaux

indicators.note: in tells us to place one piece inside the wine word that follows it

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that is all the rage in the French city of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a preposition placing the instrument in France; it is the container signal, and Bordeaux is the wine, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Lampoons that go with a bang

definitions.meaning: lampoons are short satirical attacks in writing
small fireworks that fizz and then explode

explanation.surface: Satires that make a big impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is both a short satirical piece and a small firework that bursts with a crack.

clue.text: At University this sort of research is of higher quality

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
market research is the study of consumer demand

explanation.surface: Studies done at a university are of a superior standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' is British usage for being at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket describes goods or services aimed at wealthier, more discerning buyers.

clue.text: David is last Mp to be reselected

indicators.note: to be reselected suggests these letters being chosen again and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament called David is the final one to be chosen again by his party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reselected' rearranges IS LAST MP. King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms, so he is the archetypal hymn-writer of the Bible.

clue.text: Poultry-farmer's disaster leads to redundancy

definitions.meaning: hens stopping producing eggs would ruin a chicken farmer
dismissal of workers because their jobs are no longer needed

explanation.surface: A chicken farmer's troubles lead to job losses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens that cease producing eggs, and an employer dismissing staff, are both described by the same phrase.

clue.text: Queen in trouble for parsimony

indicators.note: in tells us to place the queen inside the word for trouble

parts.note: a mess is a state of trouble
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A monarch in difficulty for being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness is stinginess with money.

clue.text: Halfway to roundabout it gives driver a better view

annotationWithheld.why: Halfway to roundabout it gives driver a better view (8) for DEMISTER: the definition is clear but no parse of 'Halfway to roundabout' builds DEMISTER, and no source gives one
annotationWithheld.clue: Halfway to roundabout it gives driver a better view

clue.text: Spanish title embracing Scottish lawyer and love poet

indicators.note: embracing means the title wraps around the lawyer and the love

parts.note: Don is a Spanish honorific for a gentleman
WS stands for Writer to the Signet, a Scottish solicitor
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman hugging a Scots lawyer and a romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Dowson was a Decadent poet of the 1890s, famous for Cynara; 'love' is both the zero and a hint at his subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Dowson wrote romantic lyrics such as Cynara, so he is a versifier of love.

clue.text: Shielded monster bearing very unusual name

parts.note: W, west, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of very are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A monster on a coat of arms carrying a strange name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles the four letters of 'very' between the bearing and the name; heraldic beasts are said to be borne on shields.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a two-legged winged dragon found on heraldic shields.

clue.text: Denied necessity to conceal gun

indicators.note: to conceal means the necessity hides the gun inside it

parts.note: a need is a necessity
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Claiming a gun had to be hidden was refuted.
explanation.definitionFit: Negated means nullified or refuted, so denied.

clue.text: Point or object of publicity for Sussex town

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass
taken as written
something everyone is talking about is the latest thing, an object of the moment

explanation.surface: Asking whether a place is notable or merely being promoted as a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthing is a seaside resort on the south coast of England in the county of West Sussex.

clue.text: Not sounding a success with the church

definitions.note: the definition is said aloud: Not sounds like knot, a kind of tie

parts.note: a hit is a success
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church failing to make an impression with a big success.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a homophone: 'Not sounding' means a word sounding like 'not', namely knot, and a hitch is a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a kind of knot used to fasten a rope to a post.

clue.text: Baking components to produce sepia

definitions.note: the clue describes what the thing does; the answer is the organ that makes the brown ink

indicators.note: components suggests the parts of the word baking being broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Ingredients mixed in baking to give a brownish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components' rearranges BAKING. Sepia is the brown ink of the cuttlefish, made in its ink sac.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuttlefish's ink sac secretes the dark fluid once used as the artist's pigment.

clue.text: Pickle and cheese taken about noon

indicators.note: taken about means the cheese goes around the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A snack of pickle and cheese eaten around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is salt water used to pickle food.

clue.text: Conciliator went in head-first in America

definitions.meaning: a peacemaker, as opposed to a hawk in politics
the American past tense of dive

explanation.surface: A peacemaker plunged into America.
explanation.definitionFit: A dove is someone favouring peace, and Americans say dove rather than dived.

clue.text: Patent on tin-opener

parts.note: over means on, as in a coat laid over a chair

indicators.note: opener here means the letter that opens the word tin

explanation.surface: A registered invention for a gadget that opens cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like a noun about inventions, but here it is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious and open to view.

clue.text: Oriental firm gives "all clear" for publication

parts.note: E, east, stands for oriental
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
no mist means visibility is all clear

explanation.surface: An Eastern company releases an all-clear statement to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The Economist is a long-running British weekly news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Economist is a weekly magazine on world affairs and business.

clue.text: Early overcoat no use to Johnson

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century style of long overcoat with a velvet collar
the Earl who failed Samuel Johnson as patron of his Dictionary, earning a famous rebuke

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned coat that the lexicographer found useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Samuel Johnson's 1755 letter scorned Lord Chesterfield for offering help only once the Dictionary was finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The coat is named after an Earl, and that same Earl was the neglectful patron Johnson rebuked.
